decision.editorial_thesis: A concise retrospective of the September 2026 CPI release should explain why the monthly and twelve-month readings answer different questions. All-items CPI rose 0.6% in September and the measure excluding food and energy rose 0.3%, both seasonally adjusted. The corresponding twelve-month increases were 3.7% and 2.6%, both not seasonally adjusted. The useful argument is to keep basket scope, time horizon and adjustment basis visible rather than turn this snapshot into a trend or policy forecast. Attribute the four reported facts to the Bureau of Labor Statistics and preserve the October 14, 2026 release date.
decision.countercase: A reader may focus on the higher monthly all-items reading, or on the lower reading excluding food and energy, as the more important signal. These four observations alone cannot establish which components caused the difference, whether inflation was accelerating or easing relative to earlier months, how the release compared with expectations, or what markets or policymakers did. Explain the difference between the measures without dismissing either or claiming that the exclusion measure proves a benign underlying trend.
decision.exception_reason: Jim decision 39 removes chart and photo minimums for analysis as well as news. Four release observations with two different horizons and adjustment bases are clearer in concise labelled text than a comparison chart that suggests a common basis. No comparable historical series or lawful contextual image is admitted. The story remains ANALYSIS; no media gap blocks its four-fact argument. Instagram delivery is skipped if an image is required by that destination.

treatment.proposed_title: September CPI: why 0.6% and 3.7% answer different questions
treatment.length_guidance: Use only the length needed to explain the four figures, approximately 250-350 words; avoid repetition or a fresh-news framing.
treatment.reader_value: Show how to read the four reported measures without confusing one month's seasonally adjusted change with the twelve-month unadjusted change, or treating a basket exclusion as a proved causal explanation.
treatment.attribution: Use one natural BLS attribution linked to the verified dated official archive. Do not add a discretionary source list, direct quotations, a ritual cutoff footer or internal workflow language.

evidence_limits: The four values remain reported actuals with their supplied September 2026 period and original release vintage; no estimate or forecast is supplied.

Do not add component drivers, historical comparisons, annualized rates, forecasts, consensus, surprises, market reactions, policy conclusions, GEX, DEMO information or trade recommendations.
No data published after the October 14 event may be presented as known at that event.
The receipt resolves the original-release verification gap for the four facts only. Missing wider context is a limit on scope, not a reason to manufacture a larger story.
